summary:
THE FILE IS REAL AND THE ARITHMETIC IS THEIRS: tests/test_fabric.py runs 8 checks / 0 failing in 2.5 s, exit 0, three runs byte-identical at md5 0ff4a88b2f2abb100bd3e6558a5bb857 (their md5, reproduced), and invariant to a hostile os.environ (FAB_BALANCE=-1 FAB_N0=1 FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=-5 RUN_SEED=999 gives the same md5). I rebuilt all twelve of their reverts from scratch with my own mirror builder and every one lands exactly as reported -- R1..R7 each FAIL their own check and NO other (8 grids checked, one FAIL each, exit 1 each), R2b fails F2's other door, P1 PASS / P2 FAIL / P3 PASS / P4 FAIL. Every quoted float reproduced to the last digit at my own re-run: grad|A|max 0.014789065346121788 -> 0.0032142375130206347 shipped and 0.014284432865679264 -> EXACTLY 0.0 on all three ae-off arms; the dead-arm gradient sum 0.013137135707438574 identical at FAB_BALANCE 0.0 / 0.01 / 5.0 while aux moves 0.48035889863967896 -> 0.4995467960834503 -> 10.074300765991211; the per-lever negative table (FAB_BALANCE 0.48848792910575867 -> -1.4413583278656006, FAB_PONDER 0.5077826380729675 -> 0.5074093341827393, FAB_EMB_VAR 0.03685825318098068 -> -0.4340698719024658, all eight guarded ones bit-identical in aux AND counters). F7's counts recount exactly: 41 leading equations, 17 distinct (gate,lever) pairs, 11 arms, all nine required pairs present. All ELEVEN path::symbol citations in the file open. Their REFUTATION of REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD's docstring HOLDS: assemble.build({'FAB_MANAGE_EVERY':'-5'}) raises UnitError out of spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows, so FAB's own guard is armed-but-unreachable.

AND THE HEADLINE CLAIM IS REFUTED, IN THE VERY REPAIR IT ADVERTISES. Their most-wanted-on-the-record finding is that F7's numeric test was untrippable, that the revert caught it, and that the sharpened consistency test now means 'a literal typed into either does not [pass]'. THAT SECOND HALF IS FALSE, and I found it by planting the same defect on the other eight gates they never reverted. Written as a bare `0` -- z_fabric's exact spelling -- the hardcoded literal is UNDETECTED on FIVE of the nine: fab.balance, fab.explore, fab.discover, fab.breadth_cap and fab.identity_round_trip all stay green with `FAB_<LEVER>=0` typed into the reason (mirrors N_balance, N_explore, N_discover, N_domfrac, N_aew: exit 0, '=== 8 checks, 0 failing ==='). The cause is mechanical: F7 searches for the printed token in `f"{gate.value} {gate.threshold}"`, the WHOLE string, which carries unrelated numbers -- fab.balance's threshold is the literal string '> 0', fab.explore's value is '0 row(s) swapped, 0 distinct cold target(s)', fab.identity_round_trip's value ends '0 embedding(s) scored'. Worse, written as `0.0` the same literal is undetected on ALL NINE, including the four that did catch the bare `0`: mirrors D_ec, D_div, D_hop, D_ind each exit 0 with all eight green, and my per-gate table shows a standalone '0.0' present in every one of the nine arithmetic strings on the arm where the reason is emitted. So the sharpened F7 is exactly as untrippable as the version they discarded, for the same defect, one character later. I ALSO BUILT AND PROVED THE REPAIR RATHER THAN ONLY NAMING THE HOLE: an arm at FAB_<lever>=-0.0 (reachable -- build refuses `v < 0.0` and -0.0 is not less than 0.0, so all nine Config fields really read -0.0 and all nine reasons really print '-0.0') plus a signed-zero comparison, with the arithmetic/token test deleted, catches the hardcoded literal on all nine gates at BOTH spellings, 18 of 18, while the shipped tree and a legitimately reformatted reason both still pass -- 20 mirrors, 'MISBEHAVING: none'. The exact edits are in unfinished. AND IT FAILS THE OTHER DIRECTION TOO: a reason that correctly prints the value it read, formatted `{ec_w:g}` instead of `{ec_w}`, makes F7 FAIL (mirror C_ec_g, exit 1) -- a correct construct flagged as a false equation, which is the spelling requirement they explicitly deny it is.

FOUR MORE THINGS NOBODY REPORTED. (1) F2's 'class claim ... run against all three states the body can be in' is two states, not three: the rows labelled 'same window as the cache' and 'inside the emb_every cadence' are BOTH step 5 with emb_every_n=1 and BOTH enter the same-window branch, which returns before any write site -- traced with an instrumented _identities. The MIDDLE branch, the only one holding the `pop.ident_graph = None` write the repair's own docstring calls 'the cheaper half', is never entered by any of the eleven cases; it is reachable, but only at FAB_EMB_EVERY>1, which this file never sets. On every one of the three guard reverts (R2, R2b and a guard-only revert) the direct half fails on the step-9 row ALONE, so two of the eleven cases carry nothing. (2) F1's twelve n>=2 shape cells assert FINITENESS only: zeroing the whole variance term for every population size but one -- deleting the anti-collapse pressure the function exists for -- passes all eight checks (mirror Z_varcov_n2_dead, exit 0), and so does silently switching the n>=2 estimator from unbiased to biased (Z_varcov_biased, exit 0). (3) F4's 'the message names the lever' assertion is untrippable for the three REVERSED levers: stripping the names out of the generated list leaves FAB_BALANCE, FAB_PONDER and FAB_EMB_VAR in the message's static prose, and my mirror Q_neg_noname reports the failure for exactly the EIGHT guarded levers and none of the three. (4) F8's 'the refusal names the lever it read it from' passes on the shipped tree only because flush_period_windows' message contains a HISTORICAL ANECDOTE about a different value ('FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=-500 built FAB.d_manage_period=Flushes(1)'); rewording that anecdote and touching nothing else makes F8 FAIL (mirror S3_msg_no_anecdote, exit 1). And on the shipped tree the D4 switch is held to nothing at all: flipping REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD to False (S1) or deleting FAB's guard outright (S2) both leave F8 GREEN, so 'holds the D4 switch to meaning something in both positions' is true only on mirrors where the assembly's refusal has also been removed.

TWO SMALLER CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD. The file's own docstring says the runpy measurement shows 'nothing in tests/ had imported this package at all' -- FALSE: running tests/test_assemble.py and tests/test_census.py under runpy leaves `fabric` AND `fabric.levers` in sys.modules. Only the narrow claim ('fabric.api' in sys.modules is False) survives, and it survives everywhere. And there are SEVEN pre-existing test files in tests/, not six: tests/test_determinism.py (61 KB) is absent from every enumeration, from the runpy premise check and from the 9.2 s timing. I ran it: it also imports no fabric module, so the conclusion is unharmed and only the arithmetic of 'six' and 'all seven files' is wrong.

SUITE AFTER, RUN BY ME: ownership 13+32 / contract 15+59 / census 8 / assemble 9 / couplings 4, 0 failing each; derive 575 oracle cases, 0 mismatches; fabric 8 checks, 0 failing. No FAIL line anywhere. 8.7 s for the supervisor's loop, 2.5 s for the new file.

findings.detail: THE CLAIM: 'for the nine the printed token must also appear, as a standalone number, in the arithmetic the same Gate prints. That is a CONSISTENCY requirement and not a spelling one: a reason and a value formatted the same way both pass, and a literal typed into either of them does not.' THE SECOND HALF IS FALSE and the file's own docstring repeats it ('a literal typed into either of them does not'). I planted z_fabric's exact defect -- a hardcoded FAB_<LEVER>=0 in the reason -- on each of the nine gates in EQUATION_GATES, one mirror per gate, one find/replace each. FIVE OF NINE ARE UNDETECTED at the bare `0` spelling: fab.balance, fab.explore, fab.discover, fab.breadth_cap and fab.identity_round_trip each exit 0 with '=== 8 checks, 0 failing ==='. Only fab.expert_choice (the one they reverted), fab.distinctness, fab.hop_sup and fab.independence fail. THE CAUSE IS MECHANICAL, not incidental: the check searches for the token in `arithmetic = f'{gate.value} {gate.threshold}'` -- the concatenation of BOTH fields -- so any unrelated standalone number in either satisfies it. Measured per gate on the all-nine-zero arm: fab.balance's arithmetic is 'balance=0.0 x warm=0.9992 > 0' (the threshold is the LITERAL string '> 0'); fab.explore's is '0 row(s) swapped, 0 distinct cold target(s) explore=0.0, computed=4 of n_live=4'; fab.discover's is '0 handover(s), 0 distinct recipient(s) cosine distance > 0.0'; fab.breadth_cap's is 'limit=0 of live_domains=3 dom_frac=0.0, dom_min=4'; fab.identity_round_trip's is 'ae_w=0.0, emb_var=1.0, 0 embedding(s) scored spawn=True, training=True, counterfactual=False'. AND AT THE `0.0` SPELLING IT IS NINE OF NINE: every one of those arithmetic strings also contains a standalone '0.0' on the arm where the reason is emitted, so `FAB_EC_W=0.0`, `FAB_DIV_W=0.0`, `FAB_HOP_SUP=0.0` and `FAB_IND_W=0.0` -- the four the bare-0 version DID catch -- all pass too. THE OTHER DIRECTION FAILS AS WELL: a reason that correctly prints what it read as `f'FAB_EC_W={ec_w:g}'` (value '0', which IS ec_w) is FLAGGED as a false equation, because '0' is not in 'ec_w=0.0 sum(use)=0.0'. So the check is a spelling requirement after all -- undersensitive to the defect and oversensitive to a correct reformat. This is the same class as the finding they call 'THE MOST USEFUL RESULT': they found one untrippable assertion, repaired it for the single gate they reverted, and shipped an assertion that is still untrippable for five of nine at the defect's own spelling and for nine of nine one character over.

findings.symbol: src/fabric/api.py::REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD -- their REFUTATION of its own docstring
findings.detail: THEIR REFUTATION STANDS AND I REPRODUCED IT INDEPENDENTLY. The docstring reads 'True is the shipped state; False lets the value through to units.Windows exactly as it did before 2026-09-04.' assemble.build({'RUN_SEED':'7','RUN_DEVICE':'cpu','FAB_MANAGE_EVERY':'-5'}) raises spine.units.UnitError from spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows ('flush_period_windows: period_windows=Windows(-5) is negative...'), because that function runs inside the coupling compute for FAB.d_manage_period (spine/assemble.py:786, dst='FAB.d_manage_period'). So no frozen Config with a negative manage_every can exist and FAB's `if REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD and every < 0:` is armed-but-unreachable through the production path; at 0, 1 and 500 the build succeeds and manage_period returns Windows(0), Windows(1), Windows(500).
